summaryTab.matchCommentary:
The Test match at Sheikh Zayed Stadium commenced with high tactical intensity as New Zealand posted 274/10 (116.1 ov) in their opening innings. In response, Pakistan countered with 348/10 (134.6 ov), setting the stage for a compelling contest of tactical endurance. Early sessions tested batting resolve against disciplined seam movement, with both attacks striving to gain the upper hand on a developing surface.

The defining turning point arrived during Century: Kane Williamson 139 (283b), which irrevocably altered the trajectory of the match. As the match progressed through its pivotal middle stages, Kane Williamson delivered a masterclass for New Zealand (228 Runs), absorbing intense pressure and tilting the momentum decisively. Crucial partnership stands and incisive bowling spells broke the opposition's resistance, shifting the control share (New Zealand 50%) and allowing New Zealand to dictate terms heading into the decisive sessions.

Entering the final innings, Pakistan faced an uphill battle under unrelenting scoreboard pressure. New Zealand's bowling unit, bolstered by WER Somerville (16 Runs & 8 Wkts), maintained relentless discipline and attacked the stumps relentlessly. Wicket clusters in the closing sessions dismantled any remaining resistance, sealing New Zealand won by 123 runs in comprehensive fashion.

Verdict: New Zealand's triumph was built on superior pressure absorption, clinical execution during critical moments, and the ability to dominate key sessions. While Pakistan produced fighting phases, New Zealand won the pivotal turning points and sustained higher tactical control across all five days to emerge as deserved victors.
